authoritative_for: What the platform says it offers, in its own names and grouping
cannot_tell_you: Whether it behaves that way, or why it exists
grading: Authoritative on intent; check against OBS, because declarations disagree with what is served (sa.readme)
examples: Docs, help centre, API schemas, sitemaps, llms.txt, changelogs, plan tables

authoritative_for: What the client actually contains: routes, operations, components, flags
cannot_tell_you: What the server allows for a given store, plan or role
grading: Strong for existence, weak for availability
examples: Route manifests, compiled GraphQL documents, served navigation trees, APKs, CLI packages, theme files

authoritative_for: What happened on a named store, plan, region, role and date
cannot_tell_you: Whether it generalises to other stores, plans or regions
grading: Strongest for behaviour; always cite the instrument it was seen with (sh.instruments)
examples: Journeys, sweeps, staff sweeps, Android walks, received emails, webhook deliveries

authoritative_for: Where to look, coverage and joins
cannot_tell_you: Anything about the platform that is not already in the bytes
grading: A finding aid only, never evidence on its own
examples: Ledgers, COVERAGE.tsv, journey catalog, staff gates

authoritative_for: Whether a feature belongs to the product class or to one vendor
grading: One more vote on commonality; read at declaration level
examples: Zid, BigCommerce, Adobe Commerce, WooCommerce docs and APIs

authoritative_for: How the same behaviour is built: data models, state machines, algorithms
cannot_tell_you: Product completeness, or what SaaS merchants actually get
grading: Strong for internals; check the fit with the product class
examples: Saleor, Medusa, Sylius, Solidus and Spree, Magento Open Source, Vendure

authoritative_for: Formats and protocols the data and APIs should follow
examples: ISO 4217, ISO 3166, GS1, schema.org, OAuth 2.0 and OIDC, WebAuthn, UBL, PCI DSS, UCP, MCP

authoritative_for: What a market requires of platforms and merchants
cannot_tell_you: How platforms implement it (Salla shows one implementation for its market)
grading: Normative; cite the instrument and its date
examples: ZATCA e-invoicing rules, PDPL, e-commerce and consumer protection law, SAMA rules

authoritative_for: What fills a slot: a payment, carrier, tax or messaging provider's contract
grading: Authoritative for the provider; changes often
examples: Payment gateway, BNPL, carrier, e-invoicing, SMS and WhatsApp provider docs

authoritative_for: What merchants add, pay for and complain about; gaps in the core
grading: Weak one by one, strong in aggregate
examples: App listings and reviews, community forums, partner sites, Wayback Machine snapshots

authoritative_for: Patterns, trade-offs, how mature teams built similar systems
grading: Strong for method; a vendor blog is one company's account
examples: Books, papers, vendor engineering blogs and talks

authoritative_for: Tacit knowledge: how merchants and operators really work
examples: Merchants, agencies, former platform engineers, support staff

authoritative_for: Feasibility, performance and cost on Sharrwah's own stack
examples: Spikes, a walking skeleton, load tests, prototypes

cannot_tell_you: Nothing about the world: a decision is not evidence
grading: Recorded with date and rationale (an ADR)
